Description: Foundational concepts of computer engineering covering digital systems, computer organisation, logic gates, and the role of computer engineers in technology-driven industries.
LearningOutcomes: Describe the fundamental components of a computer system
Explain the relationship between hardware and software in computing
Identify career pathways and professional ethics in computer engineering

Description: Study of Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential logic circuits, flip-flops, registers, counters, and the design of digital systems using hardware description languages.
LearningOutcomes: Apply Boolean algebra to simplify logic expressions
Design combinational and sequential digital circuits
Implement digital systems using hardware description languages

Description: Comprehensive study of computer organisation and architecture including CPU design, instruction set architecture, memory hierarchy, pipelining, and input/output systems.
LearningOutcomes: Explain the structure and operation of modern CPU architectures
Analyse memory hierarchy and cache performance
Design and evaluate pipelined processor implementations

Description: Introduction to chemical engineering principles including material and energy balances, unit operations, process flow diagrams, and the role of chemical engineers in industry and sustainable development.
LearningOutcomes: Apply material and energy balance principles to chemical processes
Interpret process flow diagrams for chemical plants
Identify the role of chemical engineering in industrial and environmental contexts

Description: Study of thermodynamic laws, thermodynamic properties of pure substances and mixtures, phase equilibria, chemical reaction equilibrium, and applications to chemical engineering processes.
LearningOutcomes: Apply the first and second laws of thermodynamics to engineering systems
Analyse phase equilibria and thermodynamic property changes in processes
Solve chemical reaction equilibrium problems using thermodynamic principles

Description: Principles of chemical reaction kinetics and reactor design including batch, CSTR and plug flow reactors, residence time distribution, non-ideal reactors, and catalytic reaction systems.
LearningOutcomes: Determine reaction kinetics from experimental data
Design and size ideal batch, CSTR and plug flow reactors
Analyse non-ideal reactor behaviour using residence time distribution methods

Description: Introduction to management theories and practice covering planning, organising, leading and controlling, organisational structures, and ethical leadership principles relevant to the Nigerian business environment.
LearningOutcomes: Explain classical and contemporary management theories and their applications
Apply the four functions of management to organisational scenarios
Demonstrate ethical and value-driven leadership principles in business contexts

Description: Study of marketing concepts and strategy including market analysis, consumer behaviour, product development, pricing, promotion, distribution, and digital marketing with focus on the African market context.
LearningOutcomes: Conduct market analysis and identify target segments in African markets
Develop a comprehensive marketing mix strategy for a product or service
Evaluate the impact of digital marketing tools on contemporary business growth

Description: Advanced study of strategic management processes including environmental scanning, strategy formulation, competitive analysis, strategy implementation, and evaluation with case studies from Nigerian and global organisations.
LearningOutcomes: Conduct strategic environmental analysis using SWOT, PESTLE and Porter's Five Forces
Formulate competitive business strategies for organisational growth
Evaluate strategy implementation and performance measurement frameworks
